title: Effective-resistance average trace identity and heat-kernel target
question: Can the tree-independent Gibbs-weighted effective-resistance average be rewritten exactly as the trace of the normalized Laplacian pseudoinverse, exposing an integrated heat-kernel target for the later uniform bound?

new_perspective.principle: Let D=diag(pi), W=D^(-1/2)L D^(-1/2), and u=sqrt(pi). Pairwise resistance vectors lie in u-perpendicular space. Their weighted outer-product sum is I-u u^T, so the resistance average equals tr(W^+) = sum_{k>=1} lambda_k(W)^(-1).
route: For every connected intrinsic graph, form W=D_pi^(-1/2)L D_pi^(-1/2) and its positive spectrum.
Evaluate the unordered pair resistance average directly from L^+, the transformed pair sum from W^+, and the pseudoinverse trace from the positive eigenvalues.
Check equality on every actual-likelihood row and retain the smallest positive eigenvalue, largest resistance average and identity residual as conditioning inputs.

Interpret the trace as the finite spectral integral int_0^infinity (Tr exp(-tW)-1) dt; a future uniform proof must bound this integrated heat trace on a common core, not merely one Fiedler eigenvalue.
Use directed-pair doubling, unnormalized-Laplacian trace and diagonal-q disconnected mutations as hostile controls.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: A promoted route would require a cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform bound on the normalized Green trace or integrated heat trace, plus the common-core and R-399 shell transfer obligations. The identity itself is finite and claim-nonbearing.

finite_theorem.heat_trace_identity: tr(W^+)=int_0^infinity (tr(exp(-tW))-1) dt for connected finite W
finite_theorem.normalization: The pair sum is unordered; directed-pair summation is exactly twice the trace identity

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only scalar positivity and finite inverse-spectrum bookkeeping; matrix congruence, pseudoinverse identities, Gibbs rows and all uniform or physical limits remain in the executable/open boundary.

promotion_criteria: Prove a cutoff- and volume-independent upper bound on the normalized Green trace or its integrated heat-trace representation on one Hamiltonian common core.
Control phase, source, orientation and exhaustion dependence and preserve the connected positive-spectrum hypothesis.
Transfer the trace-controlled resistance inequality to the R-399 conditional shell and combine it with the R-406 Schur decomposition before any common-alpha or GNS promotion.
stop_conditions: If the normalized Green trace diverges or the positive spectrum collapses under a validated cutoff or volume stress, retain the identity as a finite diagnostic and register the obstruction.
If directed-pair normalization, the zero mode or the D_pi congruence is mishandled, stop and record the exact failed identity.
Finite trace positivity is not a uniform, phase-selection, common-core, GNS, physical-gap or QFT theorem.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite effective-resistance trace and heat-kernel identity checkpoint only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform gap, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The trace identity changes the uniformity target from an arbitrary tree or one eigenvalue to an integrated Green/heat-kernel quantity; it does not establish a regulator or thermodynamic bound.
